bib.title: Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:1601.00670v9 [stat.CO], 9 May 2018; title page dated May 11, 2018)

question: What is variational inference, how does it approximate a posterior by optimization, and how does it compare with MCMC for statisticians?
contributions: Review mean-field VI and coordinate ascent (CAVI)
Special case of exponential-family / conditionally conjugate models
Full worked example: Bayesian mixture of Gaussians
Derive stochastic variational inference (SVI) for massive data
Survey applications, theory and open problems

results.claim: CAVI fit a 30-cluster Gaussian mixture to image histograms orders of magnitude faster than a Stan HMC/NUTS sampler.
results.metric: speed, average log predictive on held-out set
results.setup: imageCLEF color histograms (576-dim), 30 clusters, 10,000 train and 10,000 test images; compared by average log predictive of test set vs time; single comparison, not definitive
results.quote: CAVI is orders of magnitude faster than this sampling algorithm.
results.note: Authors' footnote 5: not a definitive VI vs MCMC comparison; a collapsed Gibbs sampler may do better than HMC.

results.claim: CAVI fits the mixture to ten thousand images in under a minute.
results.setup: Same imageCLEF GMM experiment, Fig 6 caption
results.quote: CAVI ﬁts a Gaussian mixture model to ten thousand images in less than a minute.

results.claim: CAVI from 10 random initializations reaches different ELBO values, so the ELBO has many local optima.
results.setup: Gaussian mixture on image data; means initialised from factorized Gaussian calibrated to data mean and variance; ELBO axis read from Fig 2 spans about -2.4e6 to -1.6e6 over 50 s
results.quote: Figure 2 shows the ELBO trajectory for 10 random initializations using the Gaussian mixture model.

results.claim: In a simulation, K = 5 two-dimensional Gaussians were recovered by CAVI; ELBO shows elbows as plateaus are reached.
results.setup: Simulated 2-D data, random means, covariances and assignments
results.quote: We simulate K = 5 Gaussians with random means, covariances, and mixture assignments.

results.claim: Mean-field variational densities generally underestimate posterior variance because KL(q||p) penalises mass where p is small.
results.quote: Further, the marginal variances of the approximation under-represent those of the target density.

results.claim: VI is faster but has no exactness guarantee; MCMC is asymptotically exact but heavier.
results.quote: MCMC methods tend to be more computationally intensive than variational inference but they also provide guarantees of producing (asymptotically) exact samples from the target density

results.claim: Where Gibbs is unavailable (mixture models) VI may beat general MCMC such as HMC even on small data.
results.quote: For mixture models where Gibbs sampling is not an option, variational inference may perform better than a more general MCMC technique (e.g., Hamiltonian Monte Carlo), even for small datasets (Kucukelbir et al., 2015).

results.claim: Relative accuracy of VI and MCMC is unknown.
results.quote: The relative accuracy of variational inference and MCMC is still unknown.

results.claim: SVI scaled LDA topic modelling to 1.8M New York Times articles.
results.setup: LDA via SVI, figure reproduced from Hoffman et al. 2013
results.quote: Figure 7 illustrates topics inferred using the latent Dirichlet allocation model (Blei et al., 2003) from 1.8M articles from the New York Times.

results.claim: Early CAVI topic models analysed thousands to tens of thousands of documents; SVI reaches millions.
results.source: Blei et al., 2003; Hoffman et al., 2013
results.quote: With SVI, topic models scale up to millions of documents

results.claim: SVI step sizes must satisfy Robbins-Monro conditions, e.g. eps_t = t^-kappa with kappa in (0.5,1].
results.setup: Stochastic natural-gradient updates for conditionally conjugate models
results.quote: Many sequences will satisfy these conditions, for example εt = t−κ for κ ∈(0.5,1].

results.claim: VI posterior mean and MLE for a Bayesian Gaussian mixture approach each other at rate O(1/n); VI covariance is too small.
results.quote: show that the asymptotic variational posterior covariance matrix is “too small”
results.note: Quote may fail if text differs; see check.

limits: Review: theory for VI is thin; each result covers one model and one variational family (Sec 5.2).
Only experiments are one simulation and one image-histogram GMM vs Stan HMC; authors say it is not a definitive VI vs MCMC comparison (footnote 5, p16).
Mean-field ignores posterior correlation and underestimates variance; CAVI finds only local optima; ELBO as model selection is not justified in theory (Sec 2.2).
Covers KL(q||p) mean-field and conditionally conjugate models; non-conjugate and black-box VI only briefly (Sec 5.3), and normalizing flows / amortised VI post-date it.
No wall-clock hardware, seeds or implementation versions for the image experiment are given.
practices: Use VI for large data and fast exploration of many models; use MCMC for small data needing precise samples (Sec 1).
Monitor convergence of CAVI by ELBO change below a small threshold, or by average log predictive on a small held-out set (Sec 2.5).
Run from several random initializations and keep the best ELBO, since the ELBO is non-convex (Sec 2.5).
Work with log probabilities and use the log-sum-exp trick with alpha = max_i x_i for numerical stability (Eq 20).
Use SVI with minibatches and Robbins-Monro step sizes to scale CAVI for conditionally conjugate models (Sec 4.3).
Do not rely on the ELBO as a model-selection criterion without caution (Sec 2.2).

terms.definition: ELBO(q) = E[log p(z,x)] - E[log q(z)]; equal to the negative KL divergence to the posterior plus log p(x); lower-bounds log evidence
latent variables mutually independent, each governed by a distinct factor: q(z) = prod_j q_j(z_j)
coordinate ascent variational inference: iteratively set q_j proportional to exp E_-j[log p(z_j|z_-j,x)] while holding other factors fixed
stochastic variational inference: stochastic natural-gradient optimisation of global variational parameters using subsampled data
conditional density of a latent variable given all other latent variables and the observations
marginal density of the observations p(x), obtained by marginalizing out latent variables
